repo_notes.content: SCOPE — what this repository is and is not. swift-pjsua is an idiomatic, Swift-only async wrapper over PJSIP's high-level C API, pjsua1. It contains no C and no C++ of its own: the PJSIP binary arrives as a SwiftPM dependency on swift-pjsip, and everything tracked here is Swift or Markdown. Two products ship from Sources/. SwiftPJSUA is the pure engine — it imports only PJSIP and Foundation and contains no CallKit, PushKit, AVAudioSession, UIKit or SwiftUI. SwiftPJSUAKit is the CallKit, PushKit and AVAudioSession orchestration that depends on the engine. The boundary between them is compiler-enforced — the engine cannot reach into the Kit — and it is the most important structural fact about this package. One directory is not about this package at all: Upstream/ holds defect reports, pasteable issue and PR drafts, and reproduction servers for pjsip/pjproject, the upstream C project, including the Swift registrars under Upstream/test-servers/. Those files document bugs in someone else's stack and the tests that prove them. Treat the whole directory as a single topic — this project's upstream-contribution programme — and do not generate pages documenting pjproject internals, individual upstream issue numbers, or the pjsua C API itself.

repo_notes.content: AUTHORITATIVE SOURCES, in precedence order. docs/Production-Roadmap.md is the canonical design record and handoff document — what was decided, why, and what remains — and supersedes any inference drawn from the code. docs/SwiftPJSUAKit-Design.md is the as-designed record for call lifecycle, media, push and CallKit deduplication, video and conferences; the as-built deltas live in the roadmap. docs/Tech-Debt.md is the register of knowingly-owed shortcuts, numbered TD-1 upward and referenced from code comments as TODO and FIXME markers; it is the honest status of the package and should not be flattened into a footnote. docs/Threading-Validation.md records the threading invariants checked against pjproject master rather than merely reasoned about. docs/Configuration-Design.md is a draft covering the configuration and credential surface. docs/Build-Bring-Up.md is the first-compile and first-run checklist. README.md is the consumer-facing entry point. Where a document and a code comment disagree, the document wins.

repo_notes.content: LOAD-BEARING INVARIANTS that any page describing the engine must convey; they are why the package has the shape it does. (1) pjsua1, the C API, was chosen over PJSUA2, the C++ one, deliberately: PJSUA2 delivers events by having you subclass its C++ classes and override virtual methods, and Swift/C++ interop can do neither, so Swift-only plus PJSUA2 would still require a hand-written C++ shim. pjsua1's events are plain C function pointers, which bridge to Swift cleanly. (2) The engine is an actor whose work runs on a custom SerialExecutor backed by ONE dedicated, PJLIB-registered POSIX thread; every blocking pjsua call goes through it, and PJSIP is never entered from GCD or from arbitrary Swift-concurrency threads. See Sources/SwiftPJSUA/Executor/. (3) thread_cnt is pinned at one or more, because pjsua's own worker threads pump events while the executor thread does not; with zero workers the callbacks silently never fire. The engine hard-sets this and it is deliberately not a public knob. (4) The C callbacks are file-private free functions that hold no reference to the actor, which makes re-entrancy impossible by construction. (5) iOS 17 or later, because custom actor executors (SE-0392) are not back-deployed below it, and iOS only, because swift-pjsip currently ships an iOS-only xcframework. (6) On iOS the app and CallKit own the audio session, not PJSIP, which is why the engine exposes an explicit audio-device API the Kit layer drives. (7) The package is in active development against an M1-to-M4 roadmap: parts marked Skeleton in source are deliberately unfinished and must be described as planned rather than as shipped behaviour. (8) Licensing is inherited, not changed here — PJSIP is GPLv2-or-later or commercial, and the binary this package links is built with bcg729 under GPLv3.
